description: Poll the status of an async job dispatched by any queued Marketo verb: the reads get_leads, get_activities, list_campaigns, list_static_lists, describe_lead_fields, list_activity_types and get_api_usage; the writes create_or_update_leads, delete_leads, merge_leads, trigger_campaign, add_leads_to_list and remove_leads_from_list; the diagnostics test_connection and check_setup; request; and the Lead Database object, asset, file and bulk verbs. Takes job_id (the value the dispatching verb's response carried). status is one of queued, processing, completed, error, or cancelled. result carries the finished job's data once status is completed (a TSV handle -- path, row_count, columns -- for the file-writing reads; date/calls_today/users for get_api_usage; per-record results, row_count and tallies for the batch writes; success and request_id for merge_leads and trigger_campaign; ok/base_url/client_id for test_connection; the reads_verified/checks/writes_unverified report for check_setup; the vendor envelope for the other verbs), and is null in every other state. error carries the classified marketo.* {code, message} once status is error, and is null in every other state. Poll again after a short delay while status is queued or processing -- there is no push notification for a direct process_call caller, only the completion_handlers routing used when the dispatching verb was called from within a flow.
embedding_description: Poll a job_id for queued/processing/completed/error/cancelled status -- how every OTHER async Marketo verb's outcome reaches a direct caller: lead and activity reads, lead writes, merges, campaign triggers, list membership changes, test_connection, check_setup, request, and the object, asset and bulk verbs. Each returns only a job_id in milliseconds; their data or vendor error arrives here.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (echoes the request), status (queued, processing, completed, error, or cancelled), result (the finished job's data once status is completed -- a TSV handle for the file-writing reads, usage numbers for get_api_usage, per-record results and tallies for batch writes, success and request_id for merge_leads and trigger_campaign, the diagnostic report for test_connection and check_setup -- null otherwise), and error (the classified marketo.* {code, message} once status is error, null otherwise). result and error are ALWAYS present keys, even when null -- never omitted for a non-terminal status.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: If status is queued or processing, say the job is still running and that the caller can check again shortly -- do not fabricate a result. If status is completed, report result's content for the dispatching verb (path/row_count for a TSV-writing verb -- and if truncated is true, say the pull is INCOMPLETE and more records may exist; date/calls_today/users for get_api_usage; tallies plus every skipped record's reasons for a batch write; success and request_id for a merge or campaign trigger; ok/base_url/client_id or the per-probe checks for a diagnostic). If status is error, report error's code and message and, for a known marketo.* class (auth_failed, permission_denied, partition_access_denied, rate_limited, invalid_params, not_configured), give the matching remediation; after a write, read the records back before any retry. If status is cancelled, say the job was cancelled and no result will arrive.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never report lead/activity/campaign/list/schema/usage data, write tallies, a merge or trigger outcome, or a diagnostic verdict unless status is completed AND result is non-null -- a queued or processing status carries neither.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Look up a previously-dispatched Marketo async job by job_id in the platform's job ledger and report its current status plus, once terminal, its result or error.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: marketo.invalid_params: job_id was missing or empty. marketo.job_not_found: no job exists with that job_id -- either it was never dispatched, the id was mistyped, or (rare) the job ledger row was purged. marketo.api_error: the platform's AsyncJobManager was not yet available when this verb ran (a plugin-startup-ordering condition, not a Marketo-side fault).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: pass the exact job_id string returned by the dispatching verb's response. marketo.job_not_found: confirm the job_id was copied correctly from the dispatching verb's response; if the dispatch call itself failed, no job exists to check -- re-invoke the dispatching verb instead of retrying this one. marketo.api_error: retry after a short delay; if it persists, the plugin's background services may not have finished starting.
